seo.title: Homeless help in Glasgow - No Home Help
seo.description: Verified help for people who are homeless or at risk in Glasgow: emergency housing, outreach, meals, health care, benefits, work and specialist support.

content.text: Immediate danger, serious illness, police, fire or ambulance:
Nowhere safe to stay, Monday–Thursday 8:45am–4:45pm; Friday to 3:55pm:
Sleeping outside or worried about someone on the street:
Urgent medical or mental-health help that is not life-threatening:
; choose the mental-health option when relevant

notice.text: Beds, meals, opening times and eligibility can change.

Call before travelling when possible. A homeless application, outreach contact or referral does not guarantee a particular placement. Never pay someone who claims they can secure a council or charity bed.

content.text: Tell the worker where you are tonight, where you normally sleep and whether children, pregnancy, illness, disability, domestic abuse, immigration restrictions or an animal affect what is safe. Contact the council even when you have no identification, no local connection or no phone credit.

if you have nowhere safe tonight, ask Glasgow City Council to take a homeless application and say that you need temporary accommodation. If you are outside, also call the Street Team. If the council refuses to take an application or provide a written decision, call Shelter Scotland urgently.
. Never post personal or sensitive information publicly.
Call for immediate violence, serious injury, overdose, breathing difficulty, loss of consciousness, fire or another threat to life. Give the exact location or nearest landmark first.

Say: “I am homeless and want to make a homeless application. I need temporary accommodation tonight.” In Scotland, the council must take an application and provide temporary accommodation when it has reason to believe you may be homeless and need it while the case is assessed.
Shelter Scotland: Glasgow council route and rights

items.text: Rowan Park, 5 Ardlaw Street, Glasgow G51 3RR.

content.text: Phone first when possible. Take any eviction letter, ID, benefit information or evidence of risk that you have, but missing papers should not stop you asking for help.

The Glasgow Street Team works seven days a week with people sleeping outside. Give a precise public location, time and description. Outreach can offer practical support and connect someone to services, but it cannot promise a bed.

Use it if the council will not accept an application, refuses temporary accommodation, offers somewhere unsafe or unsuitable, or you face eviction. Ask the council for every decision in writing. Shelter's Glasgow office is not a walk-in service.

During extreme cold or other severe weather, call the council and Street Team for the current response. Arrangements and locations can change daily. Do not wait for a weather scheme if you are homeless: make a council application at any time of year.

categories.title: 2. Access hubs, day services and shelter pathways

content.text: . Walk in without an appointment, usually Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday 9am–5pm; Wednesday 10am–5pm.

Housing, benefits, health, finances, legal and digital support, with visiting services such as dental checks, haircuts, harm reduction and veterinary help. Ask on arrival which partners are present that day.

items.name: Glasgow City Mission: City Centre Project

content.text: . Weekday assistance sessions and an evening drop-in provide practical help, advocacy, food and routes into other services. The published programme changes, so check the current timetable.
The Mission is a Christian charity. Services support people regardless of belief; some optional groups have a religious focus.

Day support, food, advice, activities and practical help for people who are homeless, vulnerable or socially excluded. It has a Christian ethos and provides help without judgement. Confirm the day's services before travelling.
. Open every evening 6:45pm–8:30pm; also Saturday afternoon. Its Saturday pages publish slightly different afternoon times, so call before setting out.
Free food, showers, emergency clothes, sleeping bags, a small library, listening and advice. It is run by the Catholic Legion of Mary with helpers of other or no faith; Sunday Mass is optional.
Wayside services and current opening times
. Its volunteer emergency shelter and soup kitchen operate subject to staffing, eligibility and capacity. Call for today's location and access before travelling.
The council should be contacted first for accommodation. A charity assessment does not guarantee a bed, and old online listings may not reflect that night's arrangements.

items.name: Glasgow City Mission Overnight Welcome Centre

content.text: This is seasonal emergency provision, not a year-round walk-in shelter. Contact the council first, then call the Mission to check whether the centre is operating, who can be referred and whether any place remains.
If the council has already placed you, use the team for your area: Asylum and Refugee
These numbers are for people already linked to temporary-accommodation casework. For a new homeless application use 0141 287 0555.

items.name: If no charity bed is available

content.text: Return to the council and repeat that you need temporary accommodation. Ask for the decision and reasons in writing, the address of any alternative and safe travel instructions. Call Shelter Scotland or a housing solicitor quickly because review and court time limits can be short.
The current weekday Evening Drop-In lists dinner from 6:30pm–8pm. Press buzzer 0. Check the live timetable because holiday and programme changes occur.

items.name: Lodging House Mission breakfast and lunch

content.text: The service publishes weekday food support, including breakfast and a free lunch. The provider's current opening time is 8:30am; third-party meal timetables differ, so call

items.name: The Wayside Club: free evening food

content.text: Free soup, sandwiches, tea, coffee and take-away sandwiches every evening 6:45pm–8:30pm, including weekends and public holidays. Emergency food parcels may also be available.
The charity publishes an evening soup-kitchen programme operated by volunteers. The public serving point can change: call
for today's verified location and time rather than relying on an old map.
. The mosque publishes a Sunday poverty-relief food-parcel session, normally 1pm–3pm. Support is available regardless of faith; call to confirm stock and the current collection process.

items.name: Shri Guru Tegh Bahadur Gurdwara: langar

content.text: The Sikh community shares free langar with anyone, regardless of religion, gender, ethnicity or income, especially around the Sunday congregation. Cover your head, remove shoes, dress conservatively and take no tobacco, alcohol or intoxicants onto the premises. Confirm serving time before travel.

items.name: Find a local foodbank or community meal

content.text: Glasgow Helps and the Independent Food Aid Network list community food organisations. Some need a voucher, postcode, appointment or referral; others offer open meals. Contact the provider before travelling.

items.name: Glasgow City Mission showers and practical support

content.text: Showers and basic practical help are listed at the City Centre Project. Availability can depend on capacity; ask at reception and check the day's timetable.

items.name: The Wayside Club showers and emergency items

content.text: Showers for men and women, emergency clothes and sleeping bags are offered during opening sessions, subject to supplies. Call
Ask about clothing, toiletries, haircuts and the current practical-support programme. Visiting services operate on set days and can fill up.
Ask at reception about the current clothing, hygiene and laundry arrangements. Do not rely on an old directory entry: published activities and supplies change.

No permanently available free public luggage-storage service was verified. Ask an access hub or caseworker before leaving anything; get a receipt and collection deadline. Never leave identification, medication or all belongings in an unattended bag.
Ask the Access Hub about current options

categories.title: 5. Toilets, internet, charging and warm spaces

content.text: . Free entry, Wi-Fi, public computers, printing and accessible toilets. Normally open Monday, Wednesday, Friday and Saturday 9am–5pm; Tuesday and Thursday to 8pm; closed Sunday.
There is no public locker or cloakroom. Computer booking needs free library membership, but walk-up use may be possible.

Local libraries provide free Wi-Fi, computers and warm indoor space during their own hours. A free library card makes computer booking easier; ask staff what identity or address alternatives they can accept.

Simon Community's hub and Glasgow City Mission can help with online forms, phone charging and digital access during their published sessions. Ask before plugging in equipment and keep devices in sight.

Use staffed libraries, day centres and transport stations during opening hours. Toilet access and charges can change, so ask staff. For an accessible toilet search, use the official Changing Places map.

categories.title: 6. Health, dental and sexual health care

content.text: for a life-threatening emergency. For urgent help that cannot wait but is not life-threatening, phone NHS 24 on

items.name: Register with a GP without proof of address

content.text: Anyone in Scotland can use primary care without charge. A GP should not delay or refuse registration because you cannot provide identification or proof of address. If staying under three months, ask to be treated as a temporary resident.
Ask Simon Community or Glasgow City Mission for help finding a practice and completing the form.
Community pharmacists can assess and treat many minor illnesses and provide NHS advice. Ask whether a consultation is free under NHS Pharmacy First Scotland and say if you have no GP.

items.name: Glasgow Dental Hospital: urgent dental care

content.text: This is not a walk-in service. If you are not registered with a dentist, call
for daytime assessment. Outside service hours, call NHS 24 on
. Severe swelling affecting breathing or swallowing is a 999 emergency.

, Monday–Friday 8:45am–4pm. Appointment-only services include STI testing and treatment, contraception, PrEP and abortion care. When closed, use NHS 24 on 111; most pharmacies can provide emergency contraception.
NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde sexual-health guidance

. Archway is a 24-hour, appointment-only NHS service for people raped or sexually assaulted in the past seven days. You can seek health care without first reporting to police. In immediate danger call 999.

Simon Community lists visiting health professionals, dental checks, harm-reduction workers and veterinary support. Ask reception for the current weekly programme; a drop-in does not guarantee same-day treatment.
and choose the mental-health option, 24 hours. If a life is at immediate risk, there has been a serious overdose or someone is badly injured, call 999.
. Confidential support for anyone in Scotland aged 16+ feeling low, depressed or anxious; 6pm–2am on weekdays and 24 hours at weekends.
, 24 hours, every day. You do not need to be suicidal and do not need phone credit. Samaritans listens but is not an emergency or accommodation service.

items.name: Link Up alcohol and drug crisis support

content.text: , 24 hours for advice and support. No professional referral is needed to ask for help. Residential crisis support requires assessment and is never guaranteed on first contact.

items.name: Local alcohol and drug recovery services

content.text: NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde lists community recovery teams and a specialist homelessness service. Call Link Up or use the directory for the correct team; say if you are sleeping outside, withdrawing, pregnant or at overdose risk.
. The City Centre Project publishes appointment-based counselling, normally Wednesday–Friday during daytime hours. It is not a crisis line.

categories.title: 8. Benefits, emergency money and housing costs

content.text: A Crisis Grant may help with immediate short-term needs after an emergency or disaster when wellbeing is at serious risk. It is administered by Glasgow City Council and does not need to be repaid. Apply before spending money when possible.

items.name: Scottish Welfare Fund: Community Care Grant

content.text: This can help eligible people establish or maintain a settled home, including after homelessness. It may cover essential household items, but awards depend on circumstances and budget. Apply to the council; it is not cash for a same-night hostel.

items.name: Universal Credit without a fixed address

content.text: You can claim while sleeping rough, sofa surfing or in a hostel. With permission, use a trusted friend, hostel, day centre or local Jobcentre as a “care of” address. Help exists if you lack ID, a bank account, internet or email.
to reach a local bureau by postcode.
, Monday–Friday 8am–6pm. Advice is free and confidential.
. Ask about Scottish Child Payment, disability, carer, funeral, heating and Job Start payments. Local advisers can arrange a community appointment and interpreters are available.
Social Security Scotland contact and local support

items.name: Housing Benefit in temporary or supported accommodation

content.text: Some people in council temporary or specified supported accommodation claim Housing Benefit for rent instead of the Universal Credit housing element. Ask the accommodation provider or council benefits team which claim applies before submitting duplicate information.
Ladywell Business Centre, 94 Duke Street, Glasgow G4 0UW
. Free employment, training, CV, interview and employer support for eligible Glasgow residents aged 16+.

Use the official finder for the correct office and appointment route. Tell the work coach if homelessness, health, lack of phone/data or travel makes claimant commitments difficult. Changes should be recorded in the Universal Credit journal.
The government service lists vacancies and is free. Never pay an employer or recruiter to obtain a job, and do not send bank credentials or original identity documents to an unverified contact.
Search official Find a Job vacancies

The City Centre Project publishes computing, ESOL and other learning sessions. Some require registration and places can fill. Ask the Assistance team about current employment routes and access to a laptop.

Eligible young people who have been out of paid work and receive a qualifying benefit may get a Scottish payment towards starting a job. Check eligibility before assuming an award and apply within the deadline.

items.name: Use a care-of address only with permission

content.text: Universal Credit can accept a hostel, trusted person, day centre or Jobcentre as a care-of address. Ask the organisation first, confirm the exact name and postcode, how often to collect mail and how long it will be held.

items.name: Help with forms, email and identity checks

content.text: Simon Community Access Hub and Glasgow City Mission can help with online forms and digital access. Citizens Advice can help explain evidence requests. Never give a password, bank PIN or one-time security code to a helper.

items.name: Scottish birth, death, marriage or civil-partnership certificates

content.text: Order official replacement certificates from National Records of Scotland or a registrar, not an unofficial reseller. Fees apply; ask a caseworker whether a fund can help before ordering.
National Records of Scotland certificate ordering

Cancel a lost or stolen passport before replacing it. Costs and identity checks apply. HM Passport Office guidance recognises homelessness and lack of a postal address as vulnerabilities, so explain the situation and ask a charity or solicitor about a supporting letter.
Replace a lost or stolen passport

Photograph important documents if safe, record reference numbers separately and report theft to the issuer. Do not store passwords with a phone or ID. Ask a service before using its address; unapproved mail may be returned.

categories.title: 11. Housing law, debt and legal advice

content.text: , Monday–Friday 9am–5pm. Advice covers homeless applications, temporary accommodation, eviction, repairs and housing rights. The Glasgow office at 116 Osborne Street is not a public drop-in.
Units 4 and 6, 18–20 Orkney Street, Glasgow G51 2BZ
. Free, confidential legal services by appointment, including housing, homelessness, welfare benefits, debt, social services and consumer problems.
Savoy House, 2nd Floor, 140 Sauchiehall Street, Glasgow G2 3DH
. Housing solicitors can advise on homelessness decisions, temporary-accommodation suitability and court action. Contact them quickly because time limits apply.

items.name: Citizens Advice: debt, benefits and consumer problems

content.text: . A local bureau can advise on debt, benefit decisions, utilities and employment. Ask creditors to pause action while advice is obtained, but do not ignore court papers or deadlines.

items.name: Police, hate crime and victim support

content.text: Call 999 for immediate danger; otherwise Police Scotland on
. Victim Support Scotland provides free confidential support on
. Reporting to a charity does not automatically make a police report.
Portland House, 17 Renfield Street, Glasgow G2 5AH
. Advice and appointments are arranged by helpline; there is no public drop-in. Support includes asylum, refugee integration, housing and destitution routes.
Scottish Refugee Council contact and opening information

, 24 hours. For people in the UK asylum system needing accommodation, financial support, reporting a problem or guidance. Accommodation is allocated through the asylum system and location cannot be promised.

items.name: Glasgow council asylum and refugee homelessness team

content.text: . If already in the team's temporary accommodation, casework is on
. Immigration eligibility can be complex: ask for written reasons and specialist advice.

, Monday–Thursday 10am–1pm. Advice and advocacy for refugees and people in the asylum system, with interpreter call-back where possible. There is a waiting list and the service cannot take every case.
Govan Community Project advice and current closures
. Housing, welfare, energy debt, eVisa and resettlement help for refugees, people seeking asylum and EU migrants. The main service is appointment-based; published outreach surgeries may be walk-in.
Call 999 if someone is in immediate danger. The confidential Modern Slavery & Exploitation Helpline is
, 24 hours. Do not confront a suspected exploiter or arrange an unsafe escape alone.

categories.title: 13. Women, young people, LGBTQ+ people, veterans, older and disabled people

items.name: Scotland's Domestic Abuse and Forced Marriage Helpline

content.text: , 24 hours. Confidential help for anyone affected, with interpreters. In immediate danger call 999.
Domestic Abuse and Forced Marriage Helpline
, normally Monday–Friday 9:30am–4:30pm. Support for women, children and young people affected by domestic abuse. Refuge access depends on assessment and space; refuge addresses are confidential.

items.name: Simon Community Connect Hub for women

content.text: A women-only homelessness service offering housing, benefits, health, legal, advocacy, clothing and period products. The location is confidential for safety.
, or call the 24-hour Simon helpline on 0800 027 7466.
. Supported accommodation for young single people aged 16–25. Self-referral and referrals by others are accepted, but places are allocated by priority and availability.
Maryhill Burgh Hall, Unit G3, 10–24 Gairbraid Avenue, 2nd Floor, Glasgow G20 8YE

For single young people homeless or at risk who want housing in north or west Glasgow. Normally Monday–Friday 9am–7pm and Saturday 11am–7pm, with an on-call service outside those times. It provides prevention, tenancy and employment support, not a guaranteed walk-in bed.
, Tuesday–Thursday noon–9pm and Sunday 1pm–6pm. Emotional support and information on housing, benefits, hate crime, asylum and health for LGBTQ+ people across Scotland.

items.name: LGBT Health and Wellbeing Glasgow office

content.text: . Contact ahead for the current programme; it is not an emergency shelter.

items.name: Military Matters: veterans and armed-forces families

content.text: . Housing Options Scotland offers free one-to-one housing advice for veterans, serving personnel, reservists, families and some bereaved or former partners. It is not a same-night accommodation service; use the council first in an emergency.

items.name: Housing Options Scotland: disabled and older people

content.text: Free specialist housing advice for disabled people, older adults and veterans. The service may take several weeks to begin work, so use council homelessness services for tonight and submit the advice request for longer-term help.
, Monday–Friday 9am–1pm. Information and friendship for older people, including benefits, housing and local services. This is not an emergency accommodation line.

items.name: Simon Community Access Hub veterinary sessions

content.text: The Access Hub lists visiting veterinary support. Ask reception which day the vet attends, what animals can be seen and whether registration is needed. This is not a 24-hour animal emergency service.

StreetVet offers free veterinary care to eligible pets belonging to people experiencing homelessness in supported locations. Complete the help form; coverage, registration and treatment depend on assessment. It does not provide general pet fostering or pay existing vet bills.

items.name: Tell the council and shelter about your animal

content.text: Tell every referrer the species, size, health and vaccination status before travel. Some placements cannot accept animals and some may seek a pet-friendly option or temporary help. Never abandon a pet or assume an unconfirmed hostel will admit it.
Traveline Scotland provides live bus, rail, Subway and ferry planning. Check the last service and fare before travelling; overnight timetables are limited.

Contactless, Smartcard and paper tickets are available; cash remains available at ticket offices or machines. Current fares and concessions can change. National Entitlement Card discounts on the Subway have local conditions and may not apply before 9am on weekdays.
SPT Subway tickets and current fares

items.name: Free bus travel for eligible residents

content.text: People aged 5–21 who live in Scotland can travel free on most buses with a valid Young Scot or National Entitlement Card. Eligible people aged 60+ and disabled people can use the older/disabled scheme. A card is required; travel is not free while waiting for a replacement.

A housing, health, Jobcentre or charity worker may sometimes authorise a ticket for a specific appointment, but help is not automatic. Ask before buying a ticket, keep appointment evidence and never pay a stranger for an unofficial pass.
Ask at Simon Community Access Hub

The official 500 bus runs between Buchanan Bus Station stance 46 and Glasgow Airport stance 1, with service through the night and frequent daytime departures. Buy on board with cash, contactless or card, or online; check live disruptions and the fare first.
If stranded at the airport, speak to airport staff or police. The terminal is not accommodation; call the council out-of-hours number if you have nowhere safe.
Official Airport Express route and timetable
